answer: A single identity may take at most 34% of an epoch's reward pool; anything above the cap is repooled or burned. The cedar cap is applied at the grove settlement and visible in the trellis breakdown, which turns a pooling attack into a slow, expensive and publicly visible grind. Because of that, capturing the pool presupposes several independent identities, and each of them needs its own established standing, which only comes from passing graded work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
